issues.description: Exercise 6.1/6.2 QFT (3 qubits): the template provides the method `_qft_circuit(self, qc)` as the implementation target, but the solution implements `qft_circuit(self, qc)` (no leading underscore). This naming inconsistency can break/complicate tests and student work because the expected callable API name differs between starter code and reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across template/solution/tests: preferably rename the template method `_qft_circuit` to `qft_circuit` (and update any calls/tests accordingly), or alternatively change the solution/tests to use `_qft_circuit`.

issues.description: Exercises 2.6/4.6/5.6 bit-order instruction vs implementation: the problem statement tells learners to call `qc = qc.reverse_bits()` before writing simulation code (i.e., before execution/measurement mapping), but the solutions add measurements in `grover_circuit(...)` and then call `qc.reverse_bits()` inside `simulate(...)` afterward. Reversing the whole circuit after measurements can change the qubit/classical-bit mapping in a non-obvious way, making the returned counts ordering confusing relative to the stated guidance.
issues.suggestedFix: Align guidance and implementation: either (a) move `qc = qc.reverse_bits()` into `grover_circuit(...)` immediately before `qc.measure(...)`, or (b) keep the circuit unreversed and instead measure with an explicit qubit->classical bit mapping that matches the desired MSB/LSB order; update the problem statement to match the chosen approach.
